outcome: successful Vaginal Birth After Cesarean delivery (VBAC)
cohort: Women with a history of previous cesarean section who visited Malalai Obstetrics and Gynecology Hospital in Kabul, Afghanistan between March 21 and September 22, 2023.
finding: Among 567 women, 79.2% had a successful VBAC, and factors associated with success included lower gestational age, absence of gestational hypertension, cervical dilation > 4 cm, effacement >= 50% on admission, and absence of fetal distress.
mod_finding: The study found a high successful VBAC rate of 79.2%, indicating the likelihood of vaginal delivery after a previous cesarean section.
gest_age: Gestational age was identified as a factor associated with VBAC success, with lower gestational age being predictive of success.
